title: SQL-to-CSV failures are logged but exit successfully

evidence.quote: Input is read through createReadStream inside main.

reasoning: If main rejects, for example because the input SQL file cannot be read, the catch handler only logs the error and leaves process.exitCode unset. Automation can therefore treat a failed conversion as successful and continue with missing or partial CSV artifacts.
reproduction: Run sql-to-csv.ts with a missing input file; the rejection is handled by console.error without setting a non-zero exit code.
recommendation: Use a catch handler that logs the error and sets process.exitCode = 1. Also consider awaiting writer finish/error events so output failures are surfaced before success is reported.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: There are no sql-to-csv tests or spawn-based assertions for converter failure exit status.
suggestedRegressionTest: Spawn the converter with a nonexistent input file and assert status is non-zero and stderr/stdout contains the read error.
minimumFixScope: scripts/sql-to-csv.ts main catch handler, plus one CLI failure test.
